cells.tense: Right now you are the one setting the terms, and the setting is steady.
cells.ask: Offer more than the current terms ask for — time, a share, a plain favor — and let it land without an immediate counter-offer.
cells.core:
You are at the point where what passes between you is decided, and you are deciding it clearly. Not the loudest, not a passenger. You know what is yours to give and what is fair to ask, and you do not treat either as a mystery. The exchange runs. What you give is received, and what comes back to you is received too.

What holds it together is what you do after: you keep what worked and do not re-open it. Giving and getting stay in the same room here, which is rarer than it sounds. The balance is not the destination; it is what lets the next thing be offered. Keep one edge: if you start needing every exchange to come out exactly even, the same care tips. For today the work is simply to offer from the surplus you have, and let the person decide what to send back.
cells.sheetLine: You set what passes between you, and you stand behind it.
cells.verb: keeping what goes both ways even
cells.place: at the point where you decide what is shared between you

cells.tense: You're already bracing for a debt that hasn't been written yet, with the pen in your hand.
cells.ask: Let one exchange come back on its own terms today — name what you offered, then stop deciding how it should be returned.
cells.core:
What you hand over is running ahead of the moment. You are already working out the fair return before the other person has even heard you, and the working-out has become the relationship. What you are building toward is a version where nobody owes anybody and everything is clear. The strain shows in how you hold the exchange now.

This is not the same as caring too much. It is the deciding bracing against a future that has not happened. You keep trying to close the books early, and the other person can feel the pressure to settle. The stability you are protecting is real, but it is being spent on debts nobody has asked you to collect. Step back to the exchange already in front of you and let it be a gift instead of an invoice.
cells.sheetLine: You're collecting on trades that haven't happened.

cells.tense: You walked away from the trading floor and you are still standing where the door closed.
cells.ask: Sit alone for ten minutes and write down two things you are good at; then send one of them to someone you already trust.
cells.core:
The point where you set the terms is still yours to stand in, but you have been looking at it from outside. You can feel the reserved withdrawal in the body — the eye contact that cuts off early, the favor not asked for. Fair exchange is not quietly running under the surface; it is absent from your conduct of the day.

The reason is not that you cannot decide. It is that nothing lately has required you to, so the muscle has gone slack. You know what is yours and what is someone else's. What stopped is the part where you offer it and find out. The room may even be telling you to wait for permission that is not coming. The way back is not to push harder, but to sharpen one small clear judgment — what you are actually good at — and let that be the first offering.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's yours to give and you've stopped offering it.
cells.verb: keeping what goes both ways even
cells.place: at the point where you decide what is shared between you

cells.tense: You've already written what you meant to offer, and you're sitting in the room saying the page is blank.
cells.ask: Name one thing you already decided is fair between you — out loud, to the person involved — without explaining why.
cells.core:
Your hand is still on the exchange. In how you split things, what you let pass, what you quietly re-balance when someone overshoots, you are already deciding fairness between you. And you talk about the rules as if they were something that just happens to be that way. The deciding is running. The ownership of it is not.

This is not a hidden motive. It is something you do without claiming. You see what is fair before the other person does, and you shape the room accordingly, then describe yourself as someone who just goes along. That leaves the other person trading with a hand they cannot see. The way back is not to announce every move, but to claim one — one call you have already made about what is even between you — and let it be yours in daylight.
cells.sheetLine: You already set what's fair. You only haven't said it.
cells.verb: keeping what goes both ways even
cells.place: at the point where you decide what is shared between you

A reader could reasonably say the pushing is ordinary generosity. The ask survives being wrong: copying down what actually comes back is useful whether or not the bracing is the real story. The sentence that serves the writer rather than the person: ‘You are not losing by keeping score; you are losing by never letting the exchange close’ — I cut it because it is a tidy saying, not the mechanism.
